emily (CS): fyi customer Acme reporting weird rerank behavior — all returned scores are 0.0 unless we move their "query" field out of the candidate objects to the root. wondering if this is a docs/candidates vs root-query parsing bug.
emily (CS): minimal description: API 200, body contains candidates with score 0 for every item. customer says the only change that toggles it is where the query string lives.
emily (CS): attaching their simplified payload they sent: 
```json
{
  "query": "how do I reset my API key",
  "candidates": [
    {
      "id": "c1",
      "text": "Reset via settings > API keys",
      "query": "reset instructions",
      "metadata": {"source": "kb"}
    },
    {
      "id": "c2",
      "text": "Contact support to rotate keys"
    }
  ]
}
```
anna (Acme): confirmed — we tried removing the nested `query` key inside candidates and it works (non-zero scores). We thought nested keys would be ignored, not change ranking.
raj (Eng): thanks. can you paste the exact curl you used? also which rerank model/version?
anna (Acme): 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank —H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d @payload.json
# payload.json is the JSON above
```
anna (Acme): model: `rerank-v2.1`
raj (Eng): reproducing locally now. quick guess: our parser might treat candidate-level `query` as an override of the root query or as a scoring signal; if it's empty or unexpected type we default to 0.0. this could be a field-shadowing bug when both root `query` and candidate `query` exist.
support-bot: incident created automatically as INC-2024-1147 for user: Acme. assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
emily (CS): @raj can you confirm whether we return a 422 or 200? customer confused because no error returned.
raj (Eng): current behavior: returns 200 and a score array, but scores are zeros. i'll add a quick unit test to catch ambiguous `query` names.
raj (Eng): repro steps for internal: POST payload with both root `query` and candidate `query` strings -> run through scoring pipeline -> observe per-candidate scores all `0.0`. logs show "query_binding: ambiguous" in parser warnings.
raj (Eng): short-term fix: support team should tell customers to move free-text search `query` to top-level or rename nested fields to `candidate_query`/`snippet_query`. long-term: runtime should validate payload and return 422 if shadowing detected, or explicitly prefer root-level query and ignore nested `query` keys (but warn).
emily (CS): noted. I'll send Acme a repro note and suggested rename.
anna (Acme): thanks, that workaround is fine for now but would like a permanent fix.
luis (PM): can we prioritize this? impacts customer-facing correctness and is easy to trigger when KB items include a `query` attribute. tagging as P2 but moving to P1 if more customers affected.
raj (Eng): opening PR to runtime parser to reject ambiguous `query` names with a clear error + example payload. linking PR to INC-2024-1147.
raj (Eng): estimated short patch -> hotfix in ~2 business days; full compatibility plan -> longer.
emily (CS): perfect. I'll update the ticket and notify Acme with ETA and workaround. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
